event: Daily Intelligence Briefing
title: Daily Market Briefing
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Dow-led washout, semis relative bid.

The session read defensive-but-narrow: DIA -1.10% sank the tape while IWM +0.40% and QQQ +0.39% held green into Tuesday's jobless claims (fc 19.7) and Philly Fed (fc 20). Yesterday's housing cluster missed hard — permits 129.5 vs 137.7 fc, pending home sales -4.7% vs -2% fc — and oil -2.94% plus gold -3.20% confirmed a growth-scare unwind, not a rate scare. With SPY and QQQ both under their 200-DMAs, rallies are countertrend until breadth repairs.

INDICES — VIX 24.6, +4.2 over its 20-DMA; beta was sold, not bought.

Ranked: IJR +0.66%, IWM +0.40%, QQQ +0.39%, SOXX +0.28%, SPY -0.31%, DIA -1.10%. Small > large by 0.27pp. The cross-asset tell: TLT +0.84% — bonds bid alongside small caps, which is duration relief, not risk appetite.

VOLUME & BREADTH — Attention went to the hedges, not the leaders.

SPY vol_ratio 0.9x and QQQ 0.9x — both below average, so today's decline is low-conviction drift, not distribution. Real accumulation shows in SLV 1.5x and GLD 1.4x (down tape, up volume = defensive positioning); XLV 1.7x and XLE 1.5x on the sell side are distribution. Breadth diverges: adv/dec 237/264, up/down volume 0.70, only 56% above the 50-DMA and 55% above the 200-DMA, new 60d lows 39 vs 9 highs — participation is deteriorating, not confirming.

SECTORS & ROTATION — Discretionary bid, energy and health care bled.

XLY Discretionary +1.79%, XLK Technology +0.34%, XLC Comms +0.30%, XLU Utilities +0.30%, XLRE Real Estate +0.07%, XLI Industrials -0.05%, XLP Staples -0.31%, XLB Materials -0.75%, XLF Financials -1.14%, XLV Healthcare -2.20%, XLE Energy -3.27%. Top industries: UNG +5.68% and CIBR +4.72%; bottom: GDX -5.97% and SILJ -5.10%. Flows contradict price: XLP +716mm (98th pctile) and XLK +623mm (94th) are where the money went while XLU -212mm (12th) and XLC -150mm (21st) bled. Money is rotating into staples and semis hardware, out of utilities and comms — defensive risk-off, with XLV -2.20% and XLE -3.27% the weakest groups.

POSITIONING — Cheap protection, rich single-stock vol.

SPY PCR_vol 0.64 and QQQ 0.67 sit under 0.7 — complacency, while skew is positive at +10.0% and +9.6% so put premium isn't free. VIX 24.6 is well above its 20-DMA of 20.4 and VVIX 118.4 vs 106.1 says vol-of-vol is stressed. The dispersion read is the story: VIXEQ 45.2 against VIX 24.6 — a ~21-point gap means implied correlation is low; this is a stock-picker's tape, not a macro-driven one.

CROSS-ASSET — Precious metals cracking while bonds bid.

SLV -4.55% and GLD -3.20% with UUP +0.27% is dollar pressure hitting metals, not a safe-haven unwind — GDX -5.97% and SILJ -5.10% confirm the miner beta flush. Oil -2.94% after crude stocks printed 338 vs -50 fc is demand skepticism, while TLT +0.84% buys the growth-scare hedge. Next FOMC Dec 9: Polymarket prices 92% YES for a 25bp hike (5d +3pp), 7% for 50+; CME FedWatch shows 100% hike.

SIGNALS & WATCH — Fear & Greed 56.2, Neutral.

UNH -10.21% on 3.5x volume (no catalyst in headline — data-derived: mass distribution into the print) and PANW +9.90% on 2.6x are your two-sided tape; FCX -6.96% on 2.2x tracks copper at a seven-month low. Momentum is broken across factors — QUAL z=-2.09, MTUM z=-1.39, all five BEAR. Watch tomorrow: CIBR +4.72% on 2.2x (rotation confirmation, or one-day pop), GDX -5.97% on 2.2x (miner capitulation setup), and IJR +0.66% — small-cap leadership against a DIA washout is the divergence that either holds or fails.
